concern_ledger_updates.reason: The Actor supplied no new admissible evidence of a model card, launch packet, or equivalent disclosure record. Narrowing the claim to a caveated certification theory does not satisfy the policy disclosure predicate.
The Actor conceded there is no admissible evidence of approved risk acceptance. Reframing certification as bounded operational readiness does not replace the policy’s alternative compliance path.
The Actor conceded legal review is still open and produced no final legal determination or equivalent governance resolution. That preserves the unresolved compliance predicate.

final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor introduced no genuinely new admissible evidence. The response is a narrower interpretation of the same record: aggregate readiness and no severity-one rehearsal incidents may support operational launch readiness, and public governance guidance supports documenting limitations and monitoring, but those facts do not satisfy the specific release-policy requirement for a material limitation in a named launch use case. Admissible evidence still shows a 1.0-point miss in the field-service dispatch segment, that the segment is named in two enterprise deployment commitments, that legal review on disclosure remains open, and that policy requires disclosure unless the issue is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. The Actor’s caveated framing is proportionate as a description of what the packet can defensibly claim, but it is not enough for compliant_with_caveats because the caveat here is the unresolved policy condition itself, not a peripheral limitation around an otherwise satisfied rule set.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the named-use-case limitation was disclosed before launch.
No admissible evidence shows approved risk acceptance covering the unresolved dispatch gap.
Legal review remains open on whether disclosure is required.
